claims.statement: The repository is a monorepo of independently versioned packages under libs/, each with its own pyproject.toml, Makefile, and README.md, with no root pyproject.toml, so work happens inside the package being changed.
Deep Agents is layered: the deepagents harness sits on top of LangChain's create_agent, which sits on top of the LangGraph runtime; identifying which layer owns a behavior narrows where to look.

The recommended navigation heuristic is to trace from a create_deep_agent() argument to the middleware or backend it installs, then follow how that component participates during execution; missing tools point to middleware assembly and profile exclusions, while visible-but-failing tools point to backend capability and permission enforcement.

graph.py is the SDK assembly point: create_deep_agent() resolves the model and profile, resolves the backend, assembles the main-agent middleware stack, builds default and caller subagents, composes the system prompt, and delegates to LangChain's create_agent().
The deepagents package root re-exports the public surface — create_deep_agent, DeepAgentState, middleware classes, and profile registration helpers — through deepagents/__init__.py.

SDK middleware in deepagents/middleware/ can filter tools per model call, inject system-prompt context, transform messages, and maintain typed cross-turn state, which a plain tools= callable cannot do because that callable runs only after the model chooses it.

FilesystemMiddleware (middleware/filesystem.py) owns the built-in filesystem tools and the FilesystemPermission policy type, and removes the execute tool at call-time when the resolved backend does not support shell execution.
deepagents/middleware/permissions.py is a backward-compatible shim that re-exports FilesystemPermission from filesystem.py rather than defining permission logic itself.

Subagent delegation is split across two SDK middleware modules: subagents.py provides SubAgentMiddleware with declarative SubAgent and CompiledSubAgent using nested create_agent, and async_subagents.py provides AsyncSubAgentMiddleware/AsyncSubAgent for asynchronous or remote delegation.

All Deep Agents backends implement a uniform BackendProtocol defined in backends/protocol.py, and shell-capable backends implement SandboxBackendProtocol, so backends can store files in different locations behind one interface.

The backends package exposes concrete storage strategies via backends/__init__.py: StateBackend (thread-scoped default), StoreBackend, FilesystemBackend (local disk), CompositeBackend (path-prefix routing), LangSmithSandbox, LocalShellBackend, and ContextHubBackend (LangSmith Hub repo).

Profiles in deepagents/profiles/ tune the harness across two orthogonal phases: provider profiles control model construction (init_chat_model kwargs and pre-init side effects) and harness profiles control the runtime phase (prompt assembly, tool visibility, middleware, and default subagent behavior).

Built-in profiles are registered lazily via profiles/_builtin_profiles.py on first registry access (also loading third-party plugins through importlib.metadata entry points), and registry keys in the provider / provider:model form are validated by _keys.py.

deepagents-code is a prebuilt terminal coding agent built on the deepagents SDK that runs as two processes — a terminal client owning presentation/input and an agent server owning the agent runtime — connected by a streaming protocol.
In deepagents-code, cli_main is lazily imported from main.py (which owns the main loop), and the coding agent itself is constructed over create_deep_agent in agent.py.

server_graph.py exposes the make_graph() factory referenced by the generated langgraph.json for the LangGraph server, and reads configuration through ServerConfig.from_env() — the same dataclass the CLI uses to write configuration via ServerConfig.to_env().

deepagents-code configuration is layered across user, project, session, and runtime scopes, built into a single process-wide generation on first read and reused, so readers resolving through the shared resolver observe one consistent generation.

The deepagents-code tool_catalog module builds the tool list from the real bound tool objects (via a throwaway offline model and MCP discovery) rather than a hand-maintained catalog, backing both the dcode tools list CLI command and the /tools slash command.

MCP server discovery and loading in deepagents-code lives in mcp_tools.py, which loads MCP servers via langchain-mcp-adapters and auto-discovers .mcp.json configs from user- and project-level locations.

In deepagents-code the graph owns the durable per-thread cost total: CostTrackingMiddleware writes graph deltas that ride checkpoints, so cost tracking works for local, headless, and remote execution, and the client only renders the streamed total.

deepagents-code manages threads over LangGraph's built-in checkpoint persistence in sessions.py, and resume_state.py declares per-checkpoint ResumeState channels (e.g. context tokens and effective model spec) that let dcode -r restore the model the resumed thread was using.

Context offload in deepagents-code is split across offload.py (storage paths for offloaded conversation history) and offload_middleware.py (CLI-specific conversation compaction/offload middleware built on the SDK summarization primitives).

deepagents-code Auto mode is a classifier-backed approval policy (auto_mode.py) whose approval-mode state is tracked per thread in a store namespace and shared between the Textual client and the agent server (approval_mode.py).

The authoritative in-repo maps are libs/ARCHITECTURE.md and libs/code/ARCHITECTURE.md for architecture, libs/DEVELOPMENT.md for workflows and repository layout, and per-package README.md files, which should be preferred over duplicated detail.

AgentServerACP adapts a compiled Deep Agent to ACP and can load persisted sessions only when the agent has a durable checkpointer; on load it restores the LangGraph thread, verifies the original working directory, and replays conversation updates to the client.

The deepagents-evals package runs behavioral agents against real LLMs and distinguishes hard-failing correctness assertions from non-failing efficiency expectations; its CLI supports runs, trials, aggregation, catalog/model-group management, and distinct exit statuses for failures, configuration errors, and unusable reports.

Talon's CLI composes configuration, persistent cron storage, selected channels, an agent runtime, and TalonHost, while Talon remains experimental and explicitly lacks production-grade isolation, complete approval policy, administrator controls, and multi-tenant boundaries.

Partner integrations are independently versioned packages, and adding one requires repository-level release, CI, change-detection, secret, labeling, and relevant sandbox workflow wiring in addition to package code and tests.
